programme.title: Wild Life of Tim Faulkner
programme.desc: Tim visits the Kimberley to witness one of natures most astounding events, discovers some subterranean hideouts, and takes Tasmanian devils to Sydney University in the quest to find a cure for a disease that threatens the species.

programme.title: Wild Life of Tim Faulkner
programme.desc: Tim travels far out west to Broome to help an old mate move a 5 metre saltwater croc to its new home. Back on the east coast Tim witnesses one of nature’s greatest sights: turtle hatchlings making their way into the sea for the first time.

programme.title: Wild Life of Tim Faulkner
programme.desc: Tim provides a countdown of the most dangerous jobs at the Australian Reptile Park before introducing us to Reggie and Russell, two orphaned kangaroo joeys he’s helping to raise.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: Trevor the Cook wants to make a comeback as a jockey and he’s hoping Milton will lend him a horse. The Wet is over and the land around Coolibah is a tinderbox, one spark and the whole country could go up in flames.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: It’s the first big muster for the season. Milton’s running three choppers in the air and an army of workers on the ground. Young Jeff wants to fly with the big boys. But he’s got to earn respect on the ground first.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: The first big muster is over, but someone didn’t make it back home. Milton sends out a search party to track down one of his most trusted workers. Raine takes Jeff on a shopping trip and on the way back…. she picks up a live crocodile.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: Milton has put a bounty on the biggest barramundi someone can catch at Coolibah. It’s an annual fishing competition.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: It’s race day: the showdown between Trevor the Cranky Cook and Milton’s sister Terry. The last time Trevor raced was in 1984, when his horse threw him in the final straight. Milton finds a massive python…that has swallowed a wallaby.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: Milton faces his worst nightmare. News is radioed through that a chopper has crashed 50km from Coolibah. He heads up a search party to find the wreckage and, hopefully, survivors.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: Milton encounters a fiery act of nature. Raine gives Little Milton a lesson about the Indigenous people of the Territory. And Milton carries out the dying wish of his mate Buckley. It’s a wake, Northern Territory style.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses
programme.desc: Little Milton goes to school. For a boy growing up as the only kid within Coo-ee, a day at school is a special event. Cristina’s not sure how her independent little cowboy will go.

programme.title: Keeping up with the Joneses

programme.title: You Cant Win Em All
programme.desc: As the Ottoman Empire collapses throughout Turkey in 1922, a number of adventurers from all over the world sign on to protect the locals from thieves and marauders--for a hefty price. Two such mercenaries are Adam and Josh, who are hired by provincial Turkish governor Osman. Adam and Josh are expected to protect their boss' gold shipment, and to provide safe conduct for Osman Bey's three daughters. Along the way, our 'heroes' decide to forget their mission and abscond with the gold, but their plans are foiled by their own inherent ineptitude--and by the bothersome interference of duplicitous Colonel Elci.

programme.title: Kids In Prison

programme.title: Kids In Prison
programme.desc: Our cameras capture two cell extractions -- one "voluntary" and one "involuntary." The "involuntary" extraction is a rare look inside a maximum-security juvenile prison as juvenile prison correctional officers make the decision to forcibly remove a teen from his cell when the teen refuses to give back a broom he has inside. A female officer tries verbal de-escalation first, to no avail. The teen is then removed by a tactical team of 7 officers wearing riot gear. In the second half of this episode, we see officers converse with a teenager in an isolation cell who requests to be put in the "time out" chair in order to get control of his anger.

programme.desc: We get unprecedented access to the process involved as two 17-year old boys arrive in a prison van to be processed into a maximum-security adult prison. Cameras capture the entire first day inside, from going through the Intake unit where they are processed in and given prison clothing, to walking the prison yard to the Youth Unit -- a cellblock inside the prison that houses all kids under the age of 18 who have been sentenced as adults in the criminal justice system. Scenes also include the boys moving into their new cell and going through the orientation interview. A 2023 update is provided at the end of the episode detailing where the boys are today.

programme.title: British Gangsters: Faces Of The Underworld
programme.desc: Villains, gangsters or 'faces' are the men who have made headlines over the past 50 years for all the wrong reasons. Some are household names, some you will not recognise, but the mere mention of these people has struck fear into entire communities. British Gangsters: Faces of the Underworld gives a unique insider's insight into these men.

programme.title: Fatal Crimes
programme.desc: Pamela Hutchinson comes to Florida to attend a friend’s funeral, but after extending her stay, she’s found dead in her condo’s bathroom. The local police launch into an investigation, unveiling a threat that spans across the country.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Ask any teenager, and he or she will tell you how tough life is: schoolwork, dating and dealing with pushy parents. But imagine having two kids while you're still in high school. Dr. Phil sits down with Corey and Kim, a troubled young couple, to see if their relationship can be saved.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Bill says he believes he is a narcissist after pushing away almost all of his loved ones, including his brother Tom and daughter Bridget, who both stopped speaking to him. After a tense reunion with Tom, Bill gets emotional when Dr. Phil reunites him with Bridget. After violent fights, cruel words, and selfish behavior, will Bill start taking accountability and change?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: You hear about scams all the time - e-mails and voicemails claiming you have won valuable prizes. Dr. Phil is outraged by what some scammers are doing to him, his family and his viewers. One website offers a Dr. Phil quiz to win $5,000 every hour, another says it has the official Dr. Phil personality test, but even more shocking are 800 numbers that take callers' money for the promise of over the phone therapy with Dr. Phil and Robin. But these 800 numbers connect innocent victims with con artists posing as Dr. Phil staff members. The fake staffers ask anywhere from $375 to $1,000 for consultation time that obviously never takes place.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Are we raising a generation of ungrateful children? Melissa’s sisters say her sons are the most spoiled boys in North America. They get everything they want – all they have to do is whine. Melissa says her kids just like toys, and she thinks her sisters may be jealous of her lifestyle. Next, Dori admits that her 13-year-old son, Parker, is spoiled. Parker says he won't take no for an answer, and even has a strategy for getting everything he wants. Find out what's behind Dori's need to spoil Parker. Then, Joan says her 14-year-old daughter, Jacquie, is a snob, and her need for trendy clothes is turning her into a materialistic monster. Plus, Lauren spends her entire paycheck shopping, but with no money in her checking account, she’s afraid she could be headed for trouble. Her mom, Diane, says she's not worried, it's just Lauren's way of relaxing.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: A headline making story of a husband’s affair with a co-worker that led to murder. Now the wife and the mistress come face to face for the first time.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Darcy says that her sister, Jennifer’s, home is in a state of complete chaos. She says Jennifer and her husband, Ralph, have no rules, their kitchen is bare, the electricity is often shut off, and they put their needs ahead of those of their four children -- who are acting out as a result. Darcy says her nephews, 8 and 10, smoke marijuana, play with weapons and recently started a local forest fire -- and that the 10-year-old once wrote a note asking for someone to kill him in his sleep. She says her 12-year-old niece was recently called to truancy court, and her 16-year-old niece is having unprotected sex in the home with her older, live-in boyfriend. Ralph concedes that he’s struggling to provide for his family financially and has made mistakes as a parent, but says Jennifer is to blame, claiming she’s checked out as a mother. Jennifer admits she’s detached from her family, struggles with depression and has trouble maintaining the household. With this family in dire need of a resolution, Dr. Phil stages a no-nonsense intervention. Are Jennifer and Ralph willing to take the necessary steps to save their family?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Parents suspect foul play in their daughter's alleged death by suicide.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Some believe self-censorship is a big problem today, particularly in light of the idea that someone can be "canceled" for their words -- blocked from having a prominent public platform or career for sharing their opinion. Dr. Phil interviews Nate, a former Idaho police officer, who claims he was fired after making a TikTok video about NBA superstar LeBron James that went viral and has been viewed over 4 million times. Nate explains how the fall-out from the video affected him and his family, too. Dr. Phil also speaks with conservative political commentator Tomi Lahren, who says she recently had to be protected by state police from student protestors at the University of New Mexico. Greg Lukianoff, president of the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, says he believes Americans have lost the ability to discuss their differences rationally. And, Dr. Shaun Harper, founder and Executive Director of the USC Race and Equity Center, says he is firmly against hate speech and feels people need to be more mindful about the effects of their words.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Em says her husband, Shawn, has cheated on her with at least 78 women -- so why does she keep taking him back? Shawn admits to at least 20 affairs but says it’s his wife’s fault that he strays.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Terrell Owens is a six-time NFL pro-bowler and arguably one of the best wide receivers to play the game, but he may be better known for his antics off the field. His tumultuous career has been well-documented, and he's been called arrogant, toxic and friendless. programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Do you ever feel nervous before posting on social media? Have you ever censored your own thoughts because you worry that you could be criticized or even canceled for posting your beliefs? Dr. Phil and his guests discuss the self-censorship debate on the internet and social media, including the fundamental misunderstanding about the true extent of “freedom of speech” under the First Amendment. Kimberly, a University of Tennessee doctoral candidate, claims her college violated her freedom of speech after a professional conduct committee determined that she had posted unprofessional content to her social media. What rights do colleges have to spy on personal social media posts? Also Tehran Von Ghasri, a comedian who performs on college campuses, says cancel culture gone too far. How does the fear of being canceled affects the jokes he performs for college students or content he posts online? Alexandra, a social media influencer and business owner, says giving opinions about COVID got her censored and three accounts closed. What did she say to get canceled? Dr. Phil also talks with Attorney Robert Shibley, a Senior Fellow at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE), who says over half of Americans are not saying how they feel for fear of offending others or being canceled. Jessica Levinson, an attorney and a Clinical Professor of Law at Loyola Law School, provides an explanation on the boundaries of the First Amendment. And, Gabrielle Gambrell, a Columbia University and NYU professor, says that social media sites are obligated to monitor hate and dangerous speech. Plus, find out which emojis you are probably using right now are deemed outdated or inappropriate!

programme.desc: Jewellery knows no limits, however bold, as we discover at the Timeless Jewels show dedicated to designers. All about eau-de-vie, that well-named "water-of-life". Ski and elegance combine in perfect harmony with innovative sports fashion from Fusalp. Borrowed from the world of dance, ballet flats are now available for men.

programme.title: L'ART ET LA MATIERE-S08
programme.desc: Fashion, crafts, design, art of living... The 'French touch' at its best.

programme.title: La grande galerie de la Francophonie
programme.desc: Together with Franco-Lebanese painter Christine Safa, we look back at the highlights of the past artistic year: the incredible story of the Louvre heist, the artworks breaking all records at auction houses, and the crucial issue of art restitution... A close-up as well on the artists and exhibitions that made us dream in 2025. And let's not forget Alex Vizorek: he tells us everything you need to know about Henri Matisse.

programme.title: CHIC EN VF S09
programme.desc: The Paris Philharmonia is home to a museum dedicated to music. Vincent Garnier Pressiat's audacious fashion style permeates the French capital.

programme.title: VERSION FRANCAISE-S10
programme.desc: Exploring the Dior Gallery. The designer Alphonse Maitrepierre finds inspiration in the problems of today for a resolutely optimistic fashion style. With Viktor & Rolf, ball gowns and acres of tulle are enough to make you spin. The costume workshops at the Bordeaux Opera House light up its dancers.

programme.title: #VF
programme.desc: Fashion, design, gastronomy, lifestyle... Discover the world of French chic!

programme.title: TENDANCE XXI S10
programme.desc: The 2024-2025 autumn/winter ready-to-wear collections had everyone talking: a look back at the runway shows. Colette Maciet, renowned "head seamstress" for some of the greatest designers, publishes "Haute Couture, une vie aux côtés des plus grands couturiers". The designers from the Fashion Farm Foundation collective present the Paris fashion week.

programme.title: L'ART ET LA MATIERE-S08
programme.desc: Fashion, crafts, design, art of living... The 'French touch' at its best.

programme.title: Passe moi les jumelles S11
programme.desc: Jo Fontaine wanted to be a farmer like his father, on the family land in his village near Geneva. But at 20, he discovered sculpture, and it was an "explosion in his head", a revelation. From the outset, he chose to express himself on stone, in sometimes monumental works.

programme.title: CHIC EN VF S09
programme.desc: In her studio, plastic artist Morgane Tschiember works and experiments her chosen materials. Between fire and transparency, Thibaut Nussbaumer tames molten glass.

programme.title: Partis rouler
programme.desc: Few places have had such an impact in the cycling world as Vancouver's north shore mountains. This region called The Shore has inspired biking trail creators worldwide.

programme.title: VERSION FRANCAISE-S10
programme.desc: Architecture, art and design at the M-A30 or Museum of the 1930s. Through colourful objects Stefania di Petrillo explores the emotional dimensions of design. Junya Watanabe deconstructs fashion to build sculptural bridges between art and textile. Marion Flament takes the art of stained glass beyond its traditional borders.

programme.title: #VF
programme.desc: Fashion, design, gastronomy, lifestyle... Discover the world of French chic!

programme.title: TENDANCE XXI S10
programme.desc: Known as poor man's gold, Lison de Caunes has brought straw marquetry bang up-to-date! The iconic couture house Céline was originally created to dress little girls. A real enthusiast, Pascal Montfort collects magazines and catalogues to better understand the fashion world. All about how to wear hats and other headgear.

programme.title: L'ART ET LA MATIERE-S08
programme.desc: Fashion, crafts, design, art of living... The 'French touch' at its best.

programme.title: Passe moi les jumelles S11
programme.desc: Anouk Hutmacher is an assistant nurse who has been covering the rural territory of Haute-Veveyse for fifteen years. She goes from farm to farm, helping old people to retain their independence. More than just physical care, she offers magnificent human encounters, sometimes funny, sometimes sad.

programme.title: CHIC EN VF S09
programme.desc: The Hôtel de la Marine in Paris looks back over two hundred and fifty years of naval history. Multi-talented artist, Aurélie Galois paints industrial canvases made of rubber and small secret boxes.

programme.title: Partis rouler
programme.desc: Antoine and Alexis ride along a legendary route: the Sea to Sky Highway. In Squamish, they meet Christian Begin who takes them on a high-altitude adventure.

programme.title: VERSION FRANCAISE-S10
programme.desc: From Rubens to Degas, exploring the Pau Fine Arts Museum collections. Self-taught and Michelin-starred, at Le Grand Véfour the chef Guy Martin looks back at his gastronomic career. An uninhibited celebration of materials and colour with Rahul Mishra. Amandine Antunez masters the art of stucco marble using plant dyes.

programme.title: #VF
programme.desc: Fashion, design, gastronomy, lifestyle... Discover the world of French chic!

programme.title: TENDANCE XXI S10
programme.desc: A partnership between Dior and Mexican craftworkers produced a vibrant result that exploded onto the catwalk during Maria Grazzia Chiuri's latest runway show. All about the tribal origins of Jerusalem artichokes. An in-depth look at arts and crafts in Normandy, as celebrated by McArthurGlen Giverny. Wearing a leopard skin print.

programme.title: L'ART ET LA MATIERE-S08
programme.desc: Fashion, crafts, design, art of living... The 'French touch' at its best.

programme.title: La grande galerie de la Francophonie
programme.desc: He is one of the great comic-book authors of our time. A brilliant illustrator, author of "L'Arabe du futur" and "Les Cahiers d'Esther", he captures childhood like no one else and has transformed his personal story into a universal work. Also a director, Riad Sattouf is our guest. We also have with us one of the greatest artists of her generation, who has conquered the most prestigious museums. Éva Jospin transforms cardboard, silk or bronze into monumental forests and landscapes, with exceptional technical mastery. And then David Hockney is on show in Belgium, at the Mons Museum of Fine Arts: this is Alex Vizorek's Vizorek'xpert column!

programme.title: CHIC EN VF S09
programme.desc: From the kitchens of the greatest chefs to that of the Lucas Carton Paris, we discover the Michelin-starred career of Hugo Bourny. Decorative painter, Éloïse d'Argent brings sublime style to ceilings and walls.

programme.title: VERSION FRANCAISE-S10
programme.desc: A visit to the Domaine National de Saint-Cloud and its museum. Loose-fitting, flowing and transparent, the designer Arthur Avellano takes latex to new heights. For Yves Saint Laurent, Anthony Vaccarello returns to the roots of the brand. Stéphanie Trolez brings the art of straw marquetry to cabinetmaking.

programme.desc: French expertise relies on its creativity, virtuosity, tenacity... All about the pizza Margherita, French sake and lobsters. Concrete, metal sheeting, glass: the favourite materials used in contemporary design.
